newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Scene quiet, deals percolating for Feb.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Scene quiet, deals percolating for Feb.

text.p: Few companies are planning initial public offerings this week, but rest assured -- investment bankers are busy behind the scenes drumming up demand for deals due in late January and early February.
"The calendar will start to fill up in the next three weeks with filings," said Sheldon Sandler, managing director of corporate finance at Ladenburg Thalmann.
"There's still a lot of backlog left (from last year), and with continued strength in stocks, you can certainly expect more companies will want to go public," he said.
The IPO market is at the tail-end of a holiday nap. Last week, only a few small deals went public and only about 10 are slated for this week.
PhotoElectron Corp PECX.O and RDO Equipment Co RDO.N could be winners this week, although premiums are likely to be slim, according to IPO Aftermarket editor John Fitzgibbon.
PhotoElectron, to be underwritten by Needham, has developed a photon radiosurgery system. Fitzgibbon said the Lexington, Mass., company could rise 1/2 point at its opening.
Fargo, North Dakota-based RDO Equipment could rise between 3/4 and a point, he said.
RDO owns and operates John Deere industrial stores and agricultural stores.

RDO's revenues have grown at a compound annual rate of 33 percent over the past five fiscal years, from $71.2 million in fiscal 1992 to $223.6 million in fiscal 1996, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Although the market's pace should gradually gain momentum, even next week should be sluggish as big-name underwriters start testing the waters in 1997. Slated for next week are Merrill Lynch's HomeSide HSI.N, two deals by Hambrecht & Quist, and Doncasters Plc DCS.N by CS First Boston.

Analysts said the market should kick back into full swing by early February. "There are probably about five or six roadshows slated for this week," said Vincent Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald. "They should really start pumping out the week of February 8th."
Sandler said one industry he is looking to in 1997 for initial public offering is automobile dealerships.
"This sector seems to be picking up speed as a consolidation play .. The car side is a very exciting area because it's ... still very fragmented and could provide a stream of new companies," he said.

Overall, the IPO market continues to look good, he said: "IPO's are always going to follow generally the conditions of the stock market. Until all of the venture capitalists are flushed out, and they have a lot of money right now, there's going to be an endless supply of deals from these guys."
